body:
Quick pass on the final head `7d30af4b` — flagged ready per the repo's draft→ready law (a quick pass that confirms the gates).

- Merges with `main`: MERGEABLE / CLEAN (`upstream/main` `5fd45923` is still the branch's base — no drift).
- Quick gate, re-run fresh on that exact head tonight: align_axes 9, axis_align 10, plane_align 9, points_align 8, turn_pivot 5, ui setup_axis 9 — all green; clippy on camcraft-app + camcraft-ui: 0 warnings.
- Body checked complete (what changed / how tested / what was not exercised / `Changelog:` / `Fixes #769`); the `Changelog:` row now names PR #770.

The branch takes no further pushes from here — a late finding goes draft → fix → re-gate → ready again. Review and merge remain the maintainer's call (feat merges at the cut).

<!-- pr-reviewer: 7d30af4bf79a6b813129e5ddc5f85ac2c19b338f -->
**Verdict: Needs changes before merge.** The frame maths is sound. The head has not changed since the last review (`7d30af4b`), so the three findings from that round still stand. I checked each one again myself, on a merge with current main.

Thank you @jenhaert. `align_from_axes` is careful work: the landing is proved before anything is stored, and every refusal is named.

This is the maintainer side's first review of this PR. The earlier `pr-reviewer` comment came from another account, so I took its findings as hints and re-checked each one rather than relying on it.

**Earlier findings, re-checked at `7d30af4b` merged with `origin/main` `23c62044`**
1. **Not fixed: a structural test fails.** `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/structural.rs:259` still looks for `"Axes in the plane - pick an edge or two points"`. The row now reads `"Part axes - pick an edge or two points for +Y and +X; +Z follows by the right-hand rule"` (`setup_axis_pick.rs:30`).
   ```
   ---- egui_app::tests::structural::setup_page_alignment_rows_structure stdout ----
   panicked at crates\ui\src\egui_app\tests\structural.rs:259:92:
   the axes rows show
   ```
   Please update the assertion to the new label. AGENTS.md: a UI change updates its structural twin.
2. **Not fixed: user-visible text still names a row that no longer exists.** The face-pick refusals at `crates/ui/src/plane_pick.rs:73` and `crates/app/src/pick/plane.rs:146` tell the user "(edges set an axis: Axes in the plane)". The doc comments at `setup_plane_pick.rs:3` and `mcp/align_tools.rs:4` say the same. Please point them at "Part axes".
3. **Not fixed: MCP.** `crates/app/src/mcp/align_tools.rs:62` still calls `AlignPartToSetup::turn_in_plane`. An agent therefore cannot reach the new full-3D alignment, and for a left-handed in-plane pair the GUI and MCP now give different answers: the GUI flips the part, MCP refuses. The body acknowledges this (lines 51-52) but names no issue, and I found none. Per "Commands ship with an MCP tool", please either route the tool through `align_from_axes` or file a `source:agent` `MCP: align the part from two axis picks` issue (`area:mcp`, P1) and name it in the body.

(The earlier comment also asked for an `Effort:` line in the body. That is not an AGENTS.md law, so I am not counting it.)

**What I checked on the maths** (`crates/app/src/pick/axis.rs:162-223`)
- **Degenerate picks.** Both directions are normalised in `dir_through`. Zero-length or non-finite picks are refused by name ("the +Y pick has no length"). Picks within 1 degree of (anti)parallel, including the same edge twice, are refused by name (`:177`). No part, and faces, are refused. No NaN reaches the command: `check_location` and the finiteness check at `:216` both guard it.
- **Handedness.** `colz = cross(colx, coly)` of two unit orthogonal columns, so the stored rotation is always proper (det +1) and never a mirror. A "left-handed" pick pair turns the part over; it does not mirror the program.
- **Frame.** The primary is kept exactly and the secondary is Gram-Schmidt squared to it. The landing is re-read through the new alignment before the command is built (`:200-212`).
- **Stale toolpaths.** The result goes through the existing `AlignPartToSetup`, and the setup's part alignment is part of every operation's stamp (`operation/stamp.rs:124-129`). An operation generated before Apply therefore reads Stale, and the post's freshness law (`posting.rs:582`) holds it back. That is already pinned for this command in `axis_align`, `setup_align` and `points_align`. The stock follows or is refused by name (`commands/setup_align.rs:310-337`), and the work offset is not touched.
- **One undoable command.** The UI queues `CommandKind::AlignPartFromAxes`, which runs `AlignPartToSetup::align_from_axes`. `invert` writes back the previous alignment and stock, pinned in the UI test.
- **Laws.** No `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` in the new code. Layering is ui -> app. New and grown files are under 400 lines. Provenance lines are present. The decision file is `docs/decisions/769-align-axes.md`. The body has `Changelog:` and `Fixes #769`. No snapshot PNGs, goldens, process files, dependencies, `build.rs` or `.github` changes.

**Local results** (merge with `origin/main` `23c62044` is clean)

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| app `align_axes` | 9 passed |
| app `axis_align` / `plane_align` / `points_align` / `turn_pivot` / `setup_align` / `mcp_pick` | 10 / 9 / 8 / 5 / 9 / 4 passed |
| ui `--lib setup_axis` (CWD `crates/ui`) | 9 passed |
| ui `--lib structural` | 3 passed, **1 failed** (finding 1) |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

**Requested before merge**
1. `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/structural.rs:259`: assert the new "Part axes - ..." label.
2. `crates/ui/src/plane_pick.rs:73`, `crates/app/src/pick/plane.rs:146` (and the two doc comments): rename "Axes in the plane" to the new row name.
3. MCP: route `mcp/align_tools.rs:62` through `align_from_axes`, or file and name the `MCP:` follow-up issue.

**For the maintainer (not blocking, but please decide)**
- **Skew.** Only picks within 1 degree of parallel are refused. A secondary pick 45 or 80 degrees off square is accepted and silently squared, so the second pick moves by up to 89 degrees. The status line then reads "aligns the part: +Y and +X along their picks", which is not true for the secondary. Issue #769 says "nearly-perpendicular picks" are squared, while the decision file drops a max-skew refusal. A mis-picked chamfer edge would lay the part out by that angle with no word about it. Suggestion: refuse beyond a few degrees of skew (#706 uses 5 degrees for a similar lean), or at least name the angle in the words ("+X lands 12.3 deg off its pick").
- **Edge sense.** An edge's direction is its chain walk order, which the user does not choose; only Flip does. Two square top edges picked without Flip can therefore form a "left-handed" pair. Before this PR that was refused; now it lands the part upside down (deliberate, `a_left_handed_pair_is_honoured_literally_not_refused`). The flip is visible and undoable, and the toolpaths go stale. Still, the words under Apply would be safer if they said "turns the part over (+Z points down)" when that is what will happen.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
